newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.
White sugar futures in London closed lower following a weaker New York market. Moreover, lack of physical demand weighed on prices. March ended the day at $310.20, a $1.00 loss from Monday.

In New York raw sugar futures ended an actively-traded session weaker, but steady trade buying carried the market well off the day's lows by the close. March gave up 5 points to close at 10.49 cents/lb, while May ended 3 points lower at 10.56 cents/lb. The deferreds lost between 4 and 5 points.
Lack of physical offtake and predictions of another surplus in 1996/97 will continue to weigh on prices.

EUROPE - Near normal rainfall occurred across much of Northern Europe during the week ended October 29. Harvesting operations made normal progress. Southern and Eastern Europe received favourable dry weather for harvest. Prospects have improved slightly due to dry conditions and favourable harvesting weather.
In the former Soviet Union sugar beet areas reported near normal rainfall of 10 to 20 mm. Harvesting operations are making adequate progress, after being slowed earlier this year.

NORWAY - Sugar imports in September 1996 amounted to 15,333 tonnes, raw value, up from last year's 14,215 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first three quarters of 1996 (January/September) up to 137,905 tonnes against 124,856 tonnes in the corresponding period the previous year. Total imports in 1995 reached 173,712 tonnes, down from 192,368 tonnes imported in 1994.
Major countries of origin in the first three quarters of 1996 were Denmark with 80,809 tonnes whites against 82,813 tonnes and the United Kingdom with 31,381 tonnes compared to 26,929 tonnes.

GERMANY - The excellent sugar content of the 1996 beet crop still allows for higher production of sugar than in 1995. The total amount of the beet processed in the week ended October 25, amounted to 2.19 million tonnes, down from 2.32 million tonnes in the like period the previous year.

The cumulative tonnage of processed beet reached 10.13 million tonnes, up from last year's 9.68 million tonnes. At 17.95 per cent, sugar content is sharply up on last year's 16.66 per cent and on the 1994/95 result of 16.80 per cent.

Sugar production in the week ended October 25, was 383,425 tonnes, raw value, which brought cumulative production up to 1.67 million tonnes, up on last year's 1.46 million tonnes and also above the 1994/95 result of 1.50 million tonnes.

NEW ZEALAND - Sugar imports in September 1996 jumped to 66,682 tonnes, sharply up from last year's 22,923 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first three quarters of 1996 (January/September) up tonnes raws compared to 137,071 tonnes and 78,097 tonnes whites against 16,543 tonnes.

Cumulative sugar exports in January/September 1996 reached 14,485 tonnes, down from 16,715 tonnes exported in the like period the previous year. Total exports in calendar year 1995 amounted to 20,270 tonnes against 16,007 tonnes in 1994. The major country of destination in January/September 1996 was French Polynesia with 4,013 tonnes whites against 4,111 tonnes.
F .O. LICHT - Our first estimate of the world sugar balance 1996/97 will be released on Wednesday, October 30.

Algeria, suffering from a shortage of sugar for its domestic market in the past seven weeks, has bought 76,000 tonnes of sugar, official sources said. This brought the total bought by the country this month to over 140,000 tonnes.
Lack of hard currency had prevented Enasucre and Enapal from reaching deals with foreign suppliers, prompting an acute sugar shortage in the domestic market.
